title: Adding spatial lookups to RasterField interpolated the user-supplied band index from the lookup tuple straight into the PostGIS SQL template, so a non-integer band index injects SQL.

findings.explanation: In the getquoted() method, when handling rasters (non-geometry case), the code returns a string formatted with self.ewkb using string interpolation: "'%s'::raster" % self.ewkb. If self.ewkb is derived from user-controlled raster data without proper escaping, this could lead to SQL injection. The value comes from to_pgraster(obj) which may not properly escape special SQL characters.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that to_pgraster() properly escapes or uses parameterized queries. If self.ewkb contains user data, use parameterized query construction instead of string formatting. Consider using Binary adapter or psycopg2's escaping mechanisms for raster data.

findings.explanation: In the check_raster method, template_params are modified by string interpolation with user-influenced values. Specifically, 'ST_Polygon(%s)' % template_params['lhs'] and similar constructions directly format user data into SQL template parameters without validation. If template_params contain unsanitized raster or geometry data, this could result in SQL injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that template_params values are already properly parameterized or sanitized before wrapping them in function calls. Do not use string formatting (%) to inject expressions into SQL; instead, ensure the underlying parameterization system handles this safely or validate/escape the values explicitly.

findings.explanation: In check_raster method, band indices are injected into template_params using string formatting: '%s, %s' % (template_params['lhs'], lookup.band_lhs). If lookup.band_lhs is user-controlled and not validated, this could allow SQL injection. Band index values should be numeric and validated.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate that lookup.band_lhs and lookup.band_rhs are integers before injecting them. Use explicit type casting or assertion: ensure they are int types or raise a validation error. This prevents non-numeric band indices from reaching SQL.

findings.explanation: This file is an adapter/utility module for spatial data type handling. It does not implement any access control logic, endpoint handlers, or permission checks. It only performs data transformation on geometry/raster objects passed to it. No authorization flaws are present.

This file defines database operators for spatial queries. It contains no endpoint handlers, access control checks, or object retrieval logic that would be subject to IDOR or authorization bypasses. The code operates on database query construction, not user access control.
